Article Title: PM Modi sets Quad agenda, calls for 'concrete goals' to ensure Indo-Pacific security
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday described the Quad as a “constructive and trusted partnership” and called for concrete goals for its next phase of cooperation.Addressing US president Donald Trump, Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese, PM Modi said Manila had a special connection with the grouping, with officials from the four countries first meeting in the city in 2007. The Quad dialogue was revived there a decade later, in 2017.“It gives me immense pleasure to meet you all. Manila and Quad have shared an age-old and special bond,” PM Modi said, adding that the latest meeting in the Philippine capital marked an important milestone for the grouping.He noted that the foreign ministers of the four countries had met five times since January last year, describing this as evidence of their “political will and shared commitment” to the partnership.“For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions,” PM Modi said.The prime minister said he was confident the meeting would help set concrete goals for the next phase of cooperation. He also thanked the other leaders for their continued support and personal contributions to the partnership.During the meeting, Trump praised PM Modi, describing him as a friend and a leader respected around the world.“He is a tough man. He is my friend. He is a great leader and respected all over the world,” Trump said, adding that Washington and New Delhi had “outstanding relationships” and were coordinating closely.The Quad meeting was held on the sidelines of the Asean summit in Manila and marked the first leaders-level gathering of the four-nation grouping since September 2024.The meeting comes as Trump prepares to travel to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit and talks with Chinese president Xi Jinping. The possibility of a meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin has also been raised.The Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, has expanded its agenda beyond traditional security cooperation to include critical minerals, resilient supply chains, emerging technologies, infrastructure and disaster response.Maritime security, commercial shipping routes, access to vital minerals and cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence and semiconductors are among the key areas of interest for the grouping.Ahead of the meeting, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the Quad was not directed against any particular country, including China.For India, the summit is part of a wider diplomatic engagement with Southeast Asia. PM Modi is also attending the Asean-India and East Asia summits in Manila, where he is expected to discuss regional security, trade and connectivity.
Article Summary: Quad meeting held on the sidelines of the Asean summit in Manila. First leaders- level gathering of the four-nation grouping since September 2024. Meeting comes as Trump prepares to travel to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Article Title: Voter or candidate has no right to get a seat reserved, says SC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said no voter or candidate had a right to demand reservation of a particular constituency for the SC/ST community, and govt's decision to reserve a constituency could not be questioned if the number of reserved constituencies was proportionate to these communities' population.The petitioners had challenged govt's 2025 amendment to Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis Act, 1961. The amendment said the next general election would be treated as the starting point for rotating constituencies reserved for SC/ST communities.They alleged this wiped out the history of previous rotations and meant some constituencies that should have been reserved based on the earlier cycle would not be reserved.Also Read| Miffed lawyer questions CJI's 'integrity', advocates seek action against him Advocate Vipin Sanghi said, "Introduction of a new set of rules, by itself, cannot furnish an independent justification for disregarding the previous rotation cycle where relevant electoral territories substantially continue to exist, albeit with altered boundaries, areas or numerical designations,"A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked, "Do voters or candidates have a right to get their constituencies reserved for the SC/ST community?" It said, "No candidate or voter has a right to get a constituency reserved.What the rules provide for is that the number of seats reserved for the SC/ST community must be proportionate to their population in the state or democratic unit going to polls. It is nobody's case that the required percentage of seats have not been reserved for the SC/ST community. "The bench refused to entertain the petition and said the amended rules conformed to the constitutionally mandated reservation policy. However, it allowed the petitioners to ask the appropriate authority to consider their representations.
Article Summary: The petitioners had challenged govt's 2025 amendment to Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis Act, 1961. The amendment said the next general election would be treated as the starting point for rotating constituencies reserved for SC/ST communities. They alleged this wiped out the history of previous rotations.

Article Title: A decade out of power: Why Congress is struggling to make a comeback in Uttarakhand
Article Text:

A state that once voted out its governments

What will decide 2027?

Who leads the party in Uttarakhand?

What is its political alternative?

Can it rebuild its organisation?

"If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle."The 'Art of War' by Sun Tzu seems to perfectly encapsulate what Congress needs to understand for the upcoming Uttarakhand assembly elections.The BJP , led in the state by chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, is seeking a historic third consecutive term. At a recent event in Dehradun, Union home minister Amit Shah set an ambitious target of winning more than 65 of the state's 70 assembly seats. The Congress, meanwhile, hopes to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the government and return to power after a decade in opposition.On paper, the Congress has a substantial list of issues to take to voters. The BJP, too, faces the challenge of defending its record in a state where the pendulum of power had previously been in constant swing.But the electoral arithmetic presents a more complicated picture as we saw in 2022.BJP can lose ground and still win comfortably; Congress can make gains and still remain distant from power.So, can Congress turn voter dissatisfaction into a legitimate political direction, or will it simply reiterate its criticisms and fail to make waves?Since the state was formed in 2000, its first four assembly elections produced a change of government every five years. The Congress won 36 seats in 2002, the BJP secured 35 in 2007, the Congress edged ahead with 32 against the BJP's 31 in 2012, and the BJP swept to power with 57 seats in 2017.And then came 2022, an election that broke the pattern and highlighted BJP’s growing strength in the state. BJP won 47 of the state's 70 seats, becoming the first party to secure consecutive terms since Uttarakhand's formation.But Congress had also made gains. Compared to 2017, its performance had improved from 11 seats to 19, while its vote share rose from approximately 33.5 per cent to nearly 38 per cent.The 2024 Lok Sabha election reinforced the challenge, with the BJP winning all five parliamentary constituencies in Uttarakhand. More significantly, Congress trailed in 63 of the state's 70 assembly segments, including 14 of the 19 constituencies it had won in 2022.Following the defeat, the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee tasked former minister Nav Prabhat with assessing the party's performance. The preliminary assessment identified a familiar set of problems: infighting, poor communication and a lack of coordination among party leaders.Congress had conducted similar reviews after its defeats in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections and the 2017 and 2022 assembly elections. Yet the organisational weaknesses identified in those exercises continued to surface.Harish Rawat remains one of Congress's most recognisable figures in Uttarakhand, but his prominence has also been tied to the party's internal power struggles.Rawat was overlooked for the chief minister's post in 2002, despite the party emerging as the largest formation. After returning to power in 2012, Congress was hit by a major crisis in 2016, when nine MLAs rebelled against his government, triggering President's Rule and a prolonged political and legal battle. Several rebels later joined the BJP.The mistrust has persisted in the run-up to 2027. The controversy involving Gaurav Kumar, an alleged conman posing as Rahul Gandhi's private secretary, exposed tensions within the state unit. Bhavna Pandey alleged that Kumar demanded Rs 2–3 crore, claiming the central leadership wanted state president Ganesh Godiyal replaced. Godiyal alleged a conspiracy, while Rawat denied any political plot and called for a police probe.Personal rivalries, including Rawat's falling-out with former aide Ranjeet Rawat, have added to the uncertainty. The November reshuffle distributed key responsibilities among senior leaders, but whether it can contain competing ambitions remains unclear.Congress's challenge is to draw on Harish Rawat's experience and support base without allowing the campaign to become another contest over leadership.The Congress has sought to make women's safety and accountability central to its criticism of the government. Garima Mehra Dasauni, the party's chief spokesperson in Uttarakhand, said Congress has compiled a list of alleged crimes against women involving senior BJP leaders in the state.Dasauni also argues that the BJP's electoral success cannot be understood simply through its development claims.In her assessment, religious and communal mobilisation, alongside welfare measures, has helped the party consolidate support. She also points to the political value of ration distribution and other welfare schemes, particularly among economically vulnerable households.This raises an important question for the Congress: how does it challenge welfare politics without appearing to dismiss the benefits that people receive?Welfare politics is not new to the Congress either. The National Food Security Act, which made access to subsidised foodgrains a legal entitlement, was enacted in 2013 under the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance government. However, the BJP has made welfare delivery a key component of its electoral strategy, raising questions about how the Congress can distinguish its own welfare agenda from that of the ruling party.The challenge for Congress, political observers suggest, is not a shortage of issues to raise but the absence of a common thread that ties them together and presents voters with a clear alternative.Political scientist Hilal Ahmed explains:"The Congress is raising all these issues but they lack a narrative between them. What connects their concerns? BJP can easily answer all these separate claims."For the Congress, this creates a difficult strategic choice. It must distinguish itself from the BJP, but it cannot assume that voters will automatically respond to a campaign built around governance failures and economic grievances.Ahmed describes the Congress as having “a little bit of a victimhood mentality” and calls it “intellectually weak”. He also warns that its response to the BJP remains fragmented rather than forming a coherent and constructive critique.His assessment of the potential electoral consequences is stark: “BJP might not win but neither will Congress.”The BJP's position in Uttarakhand is stronger than the Congress's current organisational condition. Combining the appeal of PM Modi, CM Dhami’s work on ground and the promise of continuity through the double-engine government, it seeks to retain its position.The BJP will also seek to hold together a broad social coalition, while appealing to women, young voters, ex-servicemen and the Sikh community. Its reported plans for younger candidates and greater emphasis on local feedback suggest an effort to refresh its organisation.At the same time, the party is linking voter-list revision to its rhetoric around identity and belonging. At a Dehradun meeting, BJP leader Bhatt urged workers to remove those described as “infiltrators”, saying: “Only the original people of Devbhoomi should decide the government.”One of the most important arguments in Ahmed's analysis concerns the state's economic and social structure.Migration is not simply a consequence of unemployment; it also reflects the concentration of education, healthcare, transport and jobs in towns and the plains.Ahmed argues that Congress has failed to develop a convincing response to the BJP's rhetoric around identity. It could challenge the government's economic priorities and what he describes as a decade of policy paralysis, but must offer more than general claims about unemployment.The Dhami government's record offers Congress several openings: the Ankita Bhandari case and continuing questions over the alleged VIP angle, recruitment paper leaks, unemployment, migration, land rights and allegations of corruption.But identifying these vulnerabilities is easier than turning them into electoral support. Congress must show how it would address them, particularly concerns over employment, regional inequality and the protection of local land rights. The Uttarakhand Kranti Dal's attempt to revive the politics of statehood could also put pressure on Congress to articulate a stronger regional agenda.The party has begun preparing through leadership meetings, multiple Parivartan Yatras, village outreach and a campaign against the government's record.As Ahmed argues, Congress also has a lot of “professional politicians” — leaders who pursue political stature and may abandon Congress in the face of defeat, a scenario reminiscent of 2016.The BJP is approaching the election with the advantages of incumbency and a well-established organisation, but it is not without vulnerabilities.The Congress, meanwhile, has a substantial list of issues with which to challenge the government. But none of these issues will automatically produce a victory.The Congress needs to answer three questions.The art of war is also the art of elections. The Congress is yet to demonstrate that it understands both itself and its electoral 'enemy'.
Article Summary: Congress enters the 2027 Uttarakhand election with growing support but deep organisational and leadership challenges. The BJP, led in the state by chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, is seeking a historic third consecutive term. The Congress, meanwhile, hopes to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the government.

Article Text:

Security forces have killed 16 terrorists in J&K this year

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: Wanted terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, carrying a Rs 15 lakh bounty, escaped an extended security cordon in south Kashmir's Kulgam district with bullet wounds, while his aide Umar Nasir was killed in a gunfight Monday, security sources said. The duo was allegedly behind last week's attack that wounded three CRPF personnel at Mir Bazar in Kulgam.Latief, an A category terrorist, was believed to have fled into nearby forests after being hit by bullets during the gunfight. Nasir, classified as a B category terrorist, was killed and his body retrieved, police said. A woman who witnessed the operation confirmed Latief had been wounded.Monday’s gunfight broke out in the Larnoo area, around 100km south of Srinagar. Drones were deployed to scan the vast apple orchards and adjoining forests as security forces continued combing the area.A police officer said intensive searches were under way to track Latief after the November 11 attack on a CRPF post at Mir Bazar. The attack ended a prolonged lull in strikes against security forces and triggered one of the longest search operations in Kulgam. A local overground worker was arrested for allegedly facilitating the two terrorists.J&K Police DG Nalin Prabhat, Kashmir Zone IG Sujit Kumar and senior Army and security officers had been camping in Kulgam to oversee the operation. Security officers estimated that around “four to five” local terrorists remained active in the Kashmir Valley, with their identities known to intelligence agencies.Latief had been lying low for some time, possibly helping him evade surveillance until the Mir Bazar attack, an officer said. On October 5, IG Kumar had said Kashmir had just one active local terrorist of note and recruitment had stopped completely this year. Police had identified Latief, a resident of Kulgam, as the lone local terrorist.Security forces have neutralised 16 terrorists in J&K so far this year. CRPF’s J&K Zone Special DG Sandeep Khirwar described the situation in J&K as “nearing normalcy”, but acknowledged that challenges remained.
Article Summary: Wanted terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, carrying a Rs 15 lakh bounty, escaped an extended security cordon in south Kashmir's Kulgam district with bullet wounds. His aide Umar Nasir was killed in a gunfight Monday, security sources said. The duo was allegedly behind last week's attack that wounded three CRPF personnel at Mir Bazar in Kulgam.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang rape and murder case and granted them bail."Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Article Title: Missile attack targets LPG tanker with 24 Indians in Strait of Hormuz; all crew safe
Article Text:
24 Indians safe after missile attack on LPG tanker in Strait of Hormuz amid fresh ship strikes

A Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said, adding that all crew members were safe and no injuries had been reported.In a statement, Sonowal said the vessel, named TARA GAS, had a total crew of 25, including 24 Indian nationals, and that all of them were safe."On Nov 16, Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz. All 24 Indian nationals, along with the entire 25-member crew, are completely safe with no injuries. We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and well-being of our seafarers," he said in a post on X.The incident comes amid heightened maritime security concerns in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with at least four oil tankers reportedly damaged over the past 24 hours.The Iranian Navy said a fourth tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. It alleged that the vessel was navigating through a restricted maritime zone with its navigation systems switched off.In a statement carried by Iranian state broadcaster Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), the Navy's Public Relations department said the tanker had been travelling in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz with its navigation systems turned off.The Iranian Navy also warned shipping operators against entering restricted maritime areas without coordinating with the country's armed forces."The result of any illegal movement, without coordination with the armed forces, and against regulations, is encountering mines and fires," the statement said, as reported by Al Jazeera.Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency reported an attack on a tanker seven nautical miles off Khasab in Oman. All crew members were accounted for, although the extent of damage to the vessel remained unknown, the agency said.The latest incidents follow reports by Iranian naval forces that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines in and around the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday.
Article Summary: A Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16. Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said all crew members were safe and no injuries had been reported. The incident comes amid heightened maritime security concerns in and around the Strait.

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Tuesday criticised Union home minister Amit Shah for unveiling a bust of late NCP leader Ajit Pawar , calling the gesture "unfortunate". Thackeray said the BJP had earlier made Pawar's life miserable by accusing him of involvement in an alleged Rs 70,000 crore scam. He said Shah should have apologised for the allegations while paying tribute to the late leader."This (Shah unveiling Ajit Pawar's bust) was unfortunate, because Ajit Pawar's life had been made miserable (by the BJP) with the allegations of Rs 70,000 crore scam," news agency PTI quoted Thackeray as saying.He said he had expected Shah to acknowledge that the allegations against Pawar were untrue. "Ajit Pawar would have been happy had he (Shah) said these things when he was alive," he added.The former Maharashtra chief minister also responded to speculation about a possible merger between the two NCP factions. He said the decision concerned the parties involved and he would share his views only if asked.The NCP (SP), led by Sharad Pawar, is an ally of the Shiv Sena (UBT).Thackeray also called on Shah to visit Manipur, which has been affected by prolonged ethnic conflict, and Arunachal Pradesh, where he said people were fighting alongside security forces against Chinese incursions.Taking aim at the BJP-led government, Thackeray said governance and the BJP were a contradiction in terms. He also called for a change of regime, alleging that those in power only made promises.Referring to the Opposition's criticism of police action against Gen Z protesters during demonstrations over the NEET paper leak, Thackeray said Shah had failed to appear in Parliament to respond to the allegations.He also referred to the upcoming assembly elections in BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh and said voters should not forget the hardships they faced during the Covid-19 pandemic.Shah unveiled a bust of Ajit Pawar at the Zilla Parishad office in Pune on Monday. Speaking at the event, he described Pawar's death in an air crash in January as an "irreparable loss" to Maharashtra.Shah also said Pawar's work culture would serve as a "university" for future generations of political leaders.Pawar, who headed the NCP faction in the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra, died in an air crash in January 2026. His death has since triggered discussions about the political future of the two NCP factions led by Sharad Pawar and Ajit Pawar.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray criticised Amit Shah for unveiling a bust of late NCP leader Ajit Pawar. He said the BJP had earlier made Pawar's life miserable by accusing him of involvement in an alleged Rs 70,000 crore scam. Shah should have apologised for the allegations while paying tribute to the late leader, he said.

Article Title: India lost 1,765 elephants in 17 years, Karnataka 223
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: As many as 1,765 elephants died of unnatural causes in the country in the past 17 years, with casualties due to electrocution being the biggest reason, followed by train collisions, poaching and poisoning, a response of the Union environment ministry to an RTI query shows.Data shows that electrocution alone killed 1,185 elephants (a little over 67% of total casualties) during the 2009-26 period, a number which is more than five times the number of elephants killed by poaching (222). Train hits caused 277 deaths, whereas 81 elephants died of poisoning during the period.Factoring in all causes, Odisha (371) saw the highest number of elephant deaths, followed by Assam (356) and Karnataka (223).Cause-wise, the highest number of deaths due to electrocution happened in Odisha (238), followed by Karnataka (195) and Assam (191). On the other hand, Assam reported the highest number of deaths (90) due to train collisions, followed by West Bengal (68) and Odisha (45).“Electrocution is not an accident. It is negligence — illegal electric fences, sagging wires and uninsulated lines in elephant corridors. This needs to be stopped and action needed for the same,” said Amit Gupta, Noida-based environmentalist, who filed the RTI query.Though the ministry’s response to him remains silent on it, an official told TOI that deaths due to electrocution are both “accidental and intentional”. He said that, as elephants raid crops, farmers often illegally lay live electric wires to keep away ungulates and wild pigs, resulting in the deaths of elephants. He said even as the state is the sole responder, the ministry has taken steps towards minimising such deaths and mitigating wider human-elephant conflict (HEC) episodes.The ministry’s steps include a survey of sensitive stretches of railway line, a field guide (in vernacular languages as well) for mitigating HEC, identification and validation of elephant corridors, and carrying out a long-term study to know the trends, patterns and drivers of HEC in eight vulnerable states — Assam, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (phase II) — and preparation of Regional Action Plans focusing on HEC.
Article Summary: As many as 1,765 elephants died of unnatural causes in the country in the past 17 years. Electrocution was the biggest reason, followed by train collisions, poaching and poisoning.Factoring in all causes, Odisha (371) saw the highest number of elephant deaths.

Article Title: IndiGo flight to Bengaluru aborts take-off at Mangaluru Airport
Article Text:
IndiGo flight suffers technical glitch in Mangalore

MANGALURU: An IndiGo aircraft operating on the Bengaluru sector from Mangaluru aborted its take-off at approximately 6.05 pm on Monday. The aircraft, carrying 229 passengers and seven crew members, subsequently returned to the bay.Following a detailed technical inspection by the airline’s engineering team, the aircraft was declared Aircraft on Ground (AOG). All passengers subsequently deboarded.The airport and airline teams were present to assist passengers and address their queries, ensuring the necessary support was extended to them.The airline subsequently arranged a ferry flight from Bengaluru and 34 of the original 229 passengers travelled on it with the relief aircraft leaving Mangaluru Airport at 12.10am on Tuesday, said sources.A source clarified that the aircraft in question was not airborne. Two incidents of technical glitches in aircraft have been reported in the state in a single day.
Article Summary: An IndiGo aircraft operating on the Bengaluru sector from Mangaluru aborted its take-off at approximately 6.05 pm on Monday. The aircraft, carrying 229 passengers and seven crew members, subsequently returned to the bay. Two incidents of technical glitches in aircraft have been reported in the state in a single day.

NEW DELHI: At the launch of her memoir, Sonia Gandhi recalled the Congress victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections as the moment she felt accepted in India. She said her first sense of belonging came when people in her husband Rajiv Gandhi 's constituency accepted her.According to PTI, Sonia Gandhi said the 2004 election victory marked an important moment in her journey, while recalling how she gradually found acceptance in India. She also spoke about her relationship with former prime minister Indira Gandhi and the impact of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination on her family."I felt accepted when Congress won in 2004," Sonia Gandhi said, recalling the party's victory as a significant moment in her personal and political journey. She added that her first feeling of belonging came when she visited Rajiv Gandhi's constituency and people accepted her.Speaking about her relationship with former prime minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia said she was in awe of her formidable personality and initially felt intimidated by her."I was in awe of Indira Gandhi; she was formidable, I was scared of her," she said. Article Title: A US Air Force veteran who loaned his Iraq war helmet to a Wyoming veterans' post spent 11 days in jail after taking it back; prosecutors later dropped the felony theft case when they could not prove
Article Text:
Richard Knapp/Image: Cowboy State Daily

How an Iraq war helmet became the subject of a theft case

Witness statements helped establish ownership

Prosecutors drop felony charge against veteran

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What are your thoughts on how veterans' organizations handle personal artifacts? They should always allow retrieval They can impose certain rules 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A US Air Force veteran was arrested at an airport and held for 11 days after retrieving a combat helmet he had lent to a veterans' organisation in Wyoming. Prosecutors later dropped the felony theft charge after evidence emerged supporting his claim that the helmet belonged to him.Richard Knapp, 59, was arrested on July 23 at Washington Dulles International Airport while travelling with his wife and three young family members. The family had returned to the United States from the Netherlands to visit his mother and travel to several locations when authorities took him into custody.Speaking to Cowboy State Daily, Knapp said his family had no idea that a warrant had been issued against him. His wife, Nathalie, and the other family members broke down as officers took him away. "We all did," Knapp said, recalling how the family reacted to the arrest.The arrest also raised concerns about his health. Knapp requires anti-rejection medication twice a day after receiving a kidney transplant from his wife three years earlier. He said he was not given the medication while held at the Loudoun Adult Detention Center in Virginia, leaving him worried about the transplanted organ.Eight days after his arrest, Knapp was transferred to Wyoming in a three-day ground journey.He said authorities at the Laramie County jail provided his medication after he arrived in Cheyenne. Describing his experience in custody, he said, "Jail is ... jail." Court records show he was released on August 10 after posting $300 towards a $3,000 bond.Knapp served in the US Air Force for 20 years and eight months, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, according to the news outlet. During his service, he worked as a civil engineer and was assigned to a construction battalion. His advanced combat helmet was part of the equipment he used during his deployment to Iraq.After retiring, Knapp became commander of Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 4343 in Cheyenne, serving from 2015 to 2016. He allowed the organisation to display his helmet in a glass cabinet alongside other military memorabilia.Greg Anderson, who served as a fellow VFW officer during that period, told Cowboy State Daily that members had voluntarily contributed personal belongings to the display and could reclaim them whenever they wanted."All that stuff in that display case was brought in voluntarily by people," Anderson said. He added that members had the right to take their belongings back at any time.The dispute emerged in September last year, when Knapp returned to the post to collect the helmet. According to an affidavit by Laramie County Sheriff's Deputy Erin Gerhardt-Valois cited by the outlet, surveillance footage showed him opening the display cabinet, removing the helmet and attempting to leave through a side entrance. After finding the door locked, he returned to the room, picked up the helmet and left through the bar area with three companions.The incident was reported to authorities as a theft in October that year. David Stewart, the post's quartermaster, told investigators that the helmet was worth approximately $2,600. Knapp disputed the valuation, telling Cowboy State Daily that it was worth less than $400.The difference in the estimates had legal consequences. Wyoming law sets a $1,000 threshold for felony theft, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years. Theft below that amount is generally treated as a misdemeanour, punishable by up to six months in jail.The Laramie County District Attorney's Office filed a felony charge against Knapp on October 20. A warrant was subsequently issued, but Knapp said he remained unaware of it until his arrest in July 2026.The case took a different turn after investigators received statements from people who said they had witnessed Knapp bring the helmet and accompanying goggles to the VFW for display.According to the deputy's report, Knapp's friend Gary Lustgraaf told investigators that the veteran had wanted to retrieve the helmet because the post was undergoing changes and might be closing. Lustgraaf also said Knapp did not intend to take the item to the Netherlands and had left it with him.Anderson and other witnesses also provided accounts supporting Knapp's ownership of the military equipment. Stewart subsequently passed these statements to the investigating deputy on August 4, while Knapp was being transported to Wyoming.Deputy Gerhardt-Valois collected the helmet as evidence and also spoke with Knapp's family about his medical requirements. Her report noted that she contacted jail nursing staff to explain his condition.Laramie County Sheriff Brian Kozak later reviewed the investigation report and told Cowboy State Daily that it provided a complete account of the incident. He also said the deputy had made efforts to assist Knapp during the process.Knapp hired attorney Sara Lock of Just Criminal Law to represent him. He told Cowboy State Daily that he worked with his lawyer to establish the helmet's actual value and provide information supporting his ownership claim.On September 1 this year Laramie County Deputy District Attorney William Edelman filed a motion seeking dismissal of the case, stating that the prosecution could not meet its burden of proof. Circuit Court Judge Sean Chambers approved the request the following day.The dismissal ended the felony proceedings against Knapp after he had spent 11 days in custody and travelled across the country under extradition arrangements.Although the case was dropped, Knapp said the experience had affected him, particularly given his concerns about his kidney transplant and the time spent in detention. He also said he had no intention of returning to the VFW post."I'm glad I was proven innocent," Knapp told outlet. "I would never do anything like (felony theft). Never."What are your views on this story? Tell us in the comments box below.
Article Summary: Richard Knapp, 59, was arrested on July 23 at Washington Dulles International Airport while travelling with his wife and three young family members. Prosecutors later dropped the felony theft charge after evidence emerged supporting his claim that the helmet belonged to him. Knapp served in the US Air Force for 20 years and eight months.

Article Title: Construction debris, blocked tidal flows destroy nearly 30 acres of mangroves, fishing grounds along Atal Setu-NMIA corridor, environmentalists warn of damage to fish-breeding habitats
Article Text:

NAVI MUMBAI: Nearly 30 acres of mangroves and fishing grounds along the Atal Setu-Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) connectivity corridor have been destroyed due to blocked tidal flows and construction debris, environmentalists said.Officials from the Mangrove Cell, Revenue Department and CIDCO recorded the damage during a joint inspection after Nandakumar Pawar, director of Sagar Shakti and president of the Maharashtra Small Scale Traditional Fish Workers Union, raised the issue.The affected Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ)-IA stretch, along stilt bridges connecting NMIA with Atal Setu and Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), is an intertidal fishing zone. Pawar said the destruction had damaged fish-breeding habitats and threatened traditional fishing families' livelihoods. CIDCO sources said the matter was being examined.The incident comes as more than 5,000 hectares of mangroves across Maharashtra await transfer to the Forest Department under Bombay high court directions issued in 2018. The pending transfers were recorded in minutes of a meeting of the Mangrove Protection and Conservation Committee on Oct 6.Mangrove Cell sources said CIDCO controlled 1,100 hectares of mangroves, while JNPA controlled more than 250 hectares. The 2018 directions provided for mangrove protection, transfer of mangrove land to the Forest Department and formation of a committee headed by the Konkan divisional commissioner.The Mangrove Cell said it had cleared two water channels to restore tidal flow.Pawar termed the action inadequate, saying tonnes of debris remained on the mangroves. "The Maharashtra Small Scale Traditional Fish Workers Union will not hesitate to move the Bombay high court if the fishing grounds and mangrove forests are not restored," he said. B N Kumar, director of NatConnect Foundation, said connectivity projects could not ignore environmental costs or fishing communities' interests. Pawar and Kumar said similar damage had occurred elsewhere in Uran, where mangroves regenerated after tidal flow was restored and debris washed away. They said natural recovery was possible if debris was removed and tidal connectivity restored.B S Mahajan, a nature lover from Vashi, questioned why politicians were keen on constructing structures on wetlands, open spaces and other available land.
Article Summary: Nearly 30 acres of mangroves and fishing grounds have been destroyed along the Atal Setu-Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) connectivity corridor. The affected stretch, along stilt bridges, is an intertidal fishing zone. The Mangrove Cell said it had cleared two water channels to restore tidal flow.

CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has suspended five library officials over the procurement of AI-generated books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore.According to an announcement made by school education minister A Rajmohan on Sunday, those suspended are S Kamatchi, chief librarian, Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, chief librarian and information officer (in-charge), Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, librarian and information officer, Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai, and in-charge of the Periyar Arivulagam Library; S Santhana Karthikeyan, librarian and information officer, ACL, Chennai; and J Juliet, chief accounts officer, Directorate of Public Libraries.The minister said the irregularities had occurred during the previous DMK regime.The alleged irregularities came to light after writer Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 books from Agal Vilakku Pathippagam in the library’s fourth-floor Tamil section.The books reportedly carried inflated prices, AI-generated misinformation, fictitious author names and invalid International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).Writers and researchers subsequently flagged similar irregularities elsewhere.Researchers have also raised concerns about the library’s English-language books. NEW DELHI: Two people, including a three-year-old girl, were killed and four others injured after a building collapsed in east Delhi's Jwala Nagar on Tuesday morning, trapping six people under the debris.A PCR call was received at Vivek Vihar police station around 10.09am reporting the collapse in Gali Number 6, Jwala Nagar, and stating that several people were trapped.Police teams rushed to the spot and launched rescue operations with the assistance of ambulances. He then called the police emergency helpline — 100 — and confessed to the crime.Sagar Ghosh told police that he had been “out of any meaningful work” since the pandemic and was “unable to take care of his ailing mother due to his advanced age”.The accused wrote in a note to his sister, who lived with him but was not at home when their mother was killed, “I have let mother go. I have freed her. When you return home, you won’t find me either.”Sagar, who neighbours said has been struggling financially since losing his job, has been arrested.Police said the accused strangled his mother, Uma Rani Ghosh, with a white thread around 11am on the first floor of their house on Hafiz Mohammad Ishaq Road, near Behala’s Sodepur.Additional commissioner of police (I) Dip Narayan Goswami said, “The accused called up 100 and informed us about the matter. He was detained by local police and jointly questioned by the homicide section...before being arrested. Fingerprint and photography teams have collected evidence.”A preliminary investigation revealed that Uma Rani Ghosh, the victim, had been ailing for a long time, an officer said.Deputy commissioner of police (Behala) Ishani Paul said Sagar cited his inability to afford his mother’s medical and daily expenses as the trigger for his drastic decision to kill her. “It was mainly because of his old age that he was unable to look after his mother,” Paul said.Sagar lived on the first floor of the house with his mother and sister. The ground floor, also owned by them, has been rented out. Sagar’s wife and their son and daughter-in-law live elsewhere. The wife told police that she decided to live separately after Sagar allegedly hit her on her head with a hammer in 2020-21.Officers suspect the accused waited until his sister stepped out before killing their mother. “The sister left home at 9 am and returned close to noon, only to find her mother murdered,” an officer said.Forensic experts are verifying whether the note addressed to his sister was penned by Sagar.Neighbours said Sagar became reclusive after his wife left him. His speech and behavior appeared erratic frequently. At times, he would step out for walks with his mother. “He looked rather disturbed, more than his mother,” said Saikat Naha, a resident of the locality.“We are questioning the accused to know the motive behind the murder. We are trying to ascertain whether any property or personal enmity led to the killing,” said an officer.
Article Summary: Sagar Ghosh, 67, allegedly strangled his 85-year-old mother to death at their Haridevpur home on Monday morning. He then called the police emergency helpline — 100 — and confessed to the crime. Neighbours said Sagar became reclusive after his wife left him.

Article Title: Manipur shuts down over killing of 4 Tangkhul Nagas
Article Text:
A 24-hour general strike paralysed large parts of Manipur on Monday (PTI)

Guwahati:

A violent spiral

A 24-hour general strike over the Nov 13 killing of four Tangkhul Naga civilians paralysed large parts of Manipur on Monday, with police firing tear gas to disperse protesters who blocked a road in Imphal The shutdown coincided with the burial of six Liangmai Naga civilians at Naga Martyrs’ Park in Konsakhul village, more than five months after their beheaded bodies were recovered on June 10. The six had allegedly been abducted from Leilon Vaiphei village in Kangpokpi district on May 13.Their bodies had remained at the JNIMS mortuary in Imphal as their families refused to claim them until justice was delivered. The decision to proceed with the final rites was taken at a Sept 26 meeting in Guwahati involving Naga organisations, state govt representatives and the MHA.Called by the Native People’s Committee, Manipur (NPCM), the strike began at midnight and affected all five valley districts, as well as Naga-inhabited areas of Ukhrul. Markets and schools remained shut and public transport stayed off the roads, although some private vehicles operated.At Chingmeirong in Imphal East, protesters burnt tyres and demanded accountability and justice. Tensions escalated when security personnel attempted to clear the blockade.Police fired tear gas after some protesters allegedly threw stones.TheTangkhul Naga Long (TNL) separately called a 24-hour shutdown across Tangkhul areas. It blamed “Kuki terrorists”, alleged “serious lapses in security enforcement” and accused the state and central govts of failing to act against repeated targeted killings. Essential services, including electricity, water, fire, emergency and medical services, were exempted.On the Kuki side, Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) on Sunday cited the absence of “tangible solutions” from the state govt and adopted resolutions, including non-cooperation with all security forces in Kangpokpi district under the Senapati SP’s command, and the immediate deployment of village volunteers in fringe areas.CoTU will review “free movement” along NH-2 and govt activities if its demands don’t get a swift response.Its five-point charter, issued after the killing of two Kuki youths and a woman farmer at Taphou Kuki village, demands the removal of deputy CM Losii Dikho and action against NSCN-IM and ZUF-K. It also seeks removal of an alleged illegal NSCN-IM camp at Oklong in Senapati and withdrawal of forces under the Senapati SP from Kangpokpi. CoTU’s 48-hour shutdown in Kangpokpi ended at midnight on Nov 14.The Naga-Kuki conflict since Feb has claimed 71 lives — 38 from the Kuki community, including two pregnant women, and 33 Nagas, according to the figures provided. Separately, more than 300 people from the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities were killed, 49 reported missing and over 60,000 displaced in the conflict between the two communities from 2023 to 2025.
Article Summary: A 24-hour general strike paralysed large parts of Manipur on Monday. The shutdown coincided with the burial of six Liangmai Naga civilians. The six had allegedly been abducted from Leilon Vaiphei village in Kangpokpi district.

Article Title: Relationship since 2016, marriage fixed elsewhere: UP man storms woman's home, stabs her, mother and grandmother

LUCKNOW: A 26-year-old man allegedly stormed into a woman’s house and stabbed her, her mother and grandmother following a dispute over her impending marriage to another man in Bahraich late Saturday night.The accused, identified as Arzaan Qureshi, 23, was arrested by the police, Superintendent of Police Vishwajeet Srivastava told TOI.All three women sustained serious stab injuries and were rushed to the district hospital. When the woman’s younger sister opened the door, he allegedly pushed her aside and forcibly entered the house.He then attacked the woman with a knife. When her mother and grandmother rushed to intervene and rescue her, the accused allegedly attacked them as well, leaving all three seriously injured.Hearing their screams, neighbours rushed to the house, but the accused had already fled. Local residents subsequently arranged for the injured women to be taken to the district hospital for treatment.Following information about the incident, city circle officer Narayan Dutt Mishra and Dargah station house officer Amitendra Singh reached the hospital and took stock of the situation.Confirming the earlier case against Arzaan, CO City Narayan Dutt Mishra said a molestation case, along with provisions of the POCSO Act, had been registered against him six years ago.The SP subsequently confirmed to TOI that Arzaan had been arrested. Article Title: Pakistani handler used romantic relationship to recruit woman for Rajasthan Railway track blast: Probe

Accused Davinder Singh (23), and 21-year-old woman Mahakdeep Kaur

JAISALMER: The conspiracy behind the November 3 blast on a railway track near 50 GB village in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district was allegedly masterminded by a Pakistan-based ISI handler identified as Shah, who used a romantic relationship to recruit a young woman to carry out the attack.The accused were allegedly paid Rs 2.23 lakh for executing the operation, including Rs 1 lakh in cash, while the remaining amount was transferred to their bank accounts.The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar.ADGP ATS Dinesh MN, along with senior officials of AGTF, ANTF, Bikaner Range IG Om Prakash and Sri Ganganagar SP Harishankar, disclosed details of the investigation at a press conference on Sunday.The Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Sri Ganganagar police, with assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, arrested two accused, including 21-year-old Mahakdeep Kaur and Davinder Singh (23), from Gurdaspur in Punjab.Police recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and Rs 30,000 in cash from the arrested accused.Dinesh MN said the blast was carried out at the direction of a foreign-based handler whose objective was to spread panic in Sri Ganganagar and across Rajasthan.The handler allegedly provided the target location, funding and instructions for executing the attack.Investigations revealed that Mahakdeep Kaur had married around two years ago, but her marriage ended in December 2024. In February 2025, her husband, Karanveer Singh, was jailed in an NDPS case. Subsequently, he re-established contact with her and allegedly asked her to communicate with a Pakistan-based person named Lovely, who would provide money to be delivered to him in jail.Lovely later introduced her to another person identified as Shah. Gradually, conversations between Mahakdeep and Shah developed into a romantic relationship, and she became emotionally attached to him. The Pakistani handler allegedly exploited this relationship to recruit her for the railway blast and assign her targets.According to the ADGP, Mahakdeep and Davinder visited the Ramsinghpur area on October 6, but their first attempt failed because explosives were not available. They returned on October 12 or 13 with explosives and a timer, but a technical malfunction prevented the blast. Following further instructions from Pakistan, they allegedly succeeded in triggering the explosion near 50 GB on November 3. Investigators are also examining whether a train was the intended target.The breakthrough came after an extensive investigation involving the analysis of nearly five lakh call records and the questioning of more than 400 people. Police also examined suspected Pakistan-linked smugglers and their local contacts before tracing the accused through technical surveillance and human intelligence.Dinesh MN said inputs from central agencies received three days ago led ATS teams to Punjab. With assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, the suspects' locations were traced to Gurdaspur, where they were arrested on November 15.Both accused will be produced before a court and taken on remand for further interrogation to identify other members of the network and establish links with Pakistan-based handlers.
Article Summary: The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar. Police recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and Rs 30,000 in cash from the arrested accused. Mahakdeep Kaur had married around two years ago, but her marriage ended in December 2024.

Article Title: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
Article Text:
US flight chaos enters third day, over 10,000 flights hit

One router, a chain of problems: What went wrong

FAA still has no clear answer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday.He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.The trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.The technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions."We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.
Article Summary: More than 10,000 flights cancelled or delayed for third day in a row. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said things could return to normal by Monday. The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration is yet to identify the exact cause.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'

Death sentence and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: No luxury car, no horse: UP groom's JCB baraat rolls into bride's village, says inspired by CM Yogi Adityanath's bulldozer model

Article Title: A California man killed his parents after they repaid debts from his fake investment schemes, then took his children to their house to pretend to discover the bodies; he has now received two life sent
Article Text:
Mark Andre Tomas Navarrete/Image: Sacramento County Sheriff's Office

What drove Navarrete to kill his parents?

How Navarrete carried out the killings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

DNA evidence and surveillance footage helped investigators

A California man who killed his elderly parents after they helped repay debts linked to his fraudulent investment schemes has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.Mark Andre Tomas Navarrete, 46, received two consecutive life sentences from Sacramento County Superior Court Judge Michael Bowman on Friday. A jury had found him guilty of two counts of first-degree murder on Monday after prosecutors established that he killed his parents for financial gain, Sacramento County District Attorney Office said in Statement.The victims, Augusto Tacsuan Navarrete, 73, and Marjorie Jane Tomas Navarrete, 70, were killed at their home in June 2024. Prosecutors said their son stood to inherit half of their estate.Investigators found that Navarrete had been deceiving friends and relatives through fraudulent investment schemes, promising to return their money with exceptionally high interest rates.The situation became more strained when his parents began repaying family members for debts their son had accumulated. According to the attorney's office, Navarrete grew resentful of his parents and wanted their money for himself.Prosecutors said the killings were motivated by financial gain. The jury also found that Navarrete had committed multiple murders, an allegation that contributed to the sentence imposed by the court.On June 28, 2024, Navarrete drove from his home in Elk Grove to his parents' neighbourhood and left his vehicle a few blocks away, according to prosecutors.He put on a mask and gloves before travelling to their house on a kick scooter. He entered through a side gate to avoid being captured by the Ring camera installed at the front entrance.Once inside, he brought his parents into the garage, where he struck both of them on the head with an object before strangling them, prosecutors said.Navarrete then left in his parents' car and parked it a short distance from where he had initially left his own vehicle. He returned to his car on the scooter and drove away.Later that morning, he sent a text message to his parents asking whether they wanted to come over for dinner, despite knowing they were already dead, according to the attorney's office.The case took another turn when Navarrete's sister became concerned after failing to contact their parents. He subsequently went to their home with his children and pretended to discover their bodies, prosecutors said.Detectives from the Elk Grove Police Department found the kick scooter used in the journey inside Navarrete's garage. DNA testing also detected his DNA beneath his mother's fingernails, according to prosecutors.Investigators used footage from Flock cameras and other traffic surveillance systems to trace his movements on the day of the killings. The recordings helped establish parts of the route he had taken between his home and his parents' neighbourhood.The investigation also uncovered the financial circumstances surrounding the murders, including the fraudulent investment schemes and his parents' efforts to repay the resulting family debts.
Article Summary: Mark Andre Tomas Navarrete, 46, received two consecutive life sentences from Sacramento County Superior Court Judge Michael Bowman on Friday. A jury had found him guilty of two counts of first-degree murder on Monday after prosecutors established that he killed his parents for financial gain. Prosecutors said their son stood to inherit half of their estate.

Schoolchildren in the city continue to face serious safety risks as norms governing school transport are flouted with impunity, sources said. Autos, vans and other vehicles ferrying students are frequently found carrying more children than their permitted capacity, while regular inspections by the transport department and traffic police are allegedly absent.Under the Motor Vehicles Act , vehicles used to transport schoolchildren must comply with safety standards, including fixed seating capacity and adequate space for schoolbags. However, in busy areas such as Sakchi, Kadma, Mango, Bistupur and Telco, autos meant to carry four to six passengers are often seen ferrying 10 to 12 children.Overloading, coupled with rash driving and speeding, has heightened the risk of accidents. Several incidents involving school vehicles have already been reported, leaving children injured.Rising costs and the pressure to get children to school on time have forced many middle-class families to depend on private vans and autos. Parents often have little choice but to use these vehicles despite being aware of the risks.“I remain worried about my son’s safety every day, especially when I see how many children are squeezed into these autos. Due to our work commitments, we are unable to drop and pick him up from school and have to depend on these operators,” said Shiva Rao, a Bistupur resident whose son studies at a school in Kadma.Some drivers, in an attempt to make additional trips and earn more, compromise on safety. Several vehicles do not have updated documents, while fitness checks are not conducted regularly. Lack of inspections and strict enforcement has allowed the practice to continue.“Safety of children cannot be left entirely to parents and drivers. The transport department and district administration must take strict action against overloaded and poorly maintained vehicles,” said Shahid Anwar, whose daughter travels to a private school by van.District transport officer Maheshwari Prasad Yadav said a 15-day period had recently been given to school vehicle operators to complete formalities and make their vehicles compliant. “They have been asked to avoid overloading and use safe vehicles. If they fail to comply, the vehicles will be seized,” he said.He added that inspections would continue across the city and schools had been asked to counsel parents against using overloaded or unsafe vehicles.Santosh Mandal of the School Van Association said meetings would be held with drivers, school managements and transport officials to discuss safety compliance and prevent further accidents.
Article Summary: Autos, vans and other vehicles ferrying students are frequently found carrying more children than their permitted capacity. Regular inspections by the transport department and traffic police are allegedly absent. Several incidents involving school vehicles have already been reported, leaving children injured.

Article Title: Courts open, but no staff: Maharashtra's 34,000 judicial employees begin indefinite strike over pay parity
Article Text:
Around 34,000 employees from District and Subordinate Courts in Maharashtra have gone on an indefinite strike

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: Court proceedings across Maharashtra are likely to be severely affected after the Maharashtra State Judicial Employees Federation launched an indefinite strike from Tuesday, with around 34,000 employees of District and Subordinate Courts joining the protest demanding pay scales at par with high court employees.The impact was visible at the Esplanade Metropolitan Magistrate Court at CST, which usually witnesses a steady flow of cases involving central investigative agencies seeking custody of arrested accused and other legal proceedings.The court wore a deserted look, with the 37th metropolitan magistrate, DS Khedekar, seen sitting on the dais without any proceedings taking place, while lawyers waited idle in the courtroom. Court staff, meanwhile, had gathered at Azad Maidan to participate in the protest.Although the metropolitan magistrate courts will technically remain open, the absence of staff is expected to disrupt day-to-day judicial work, including remand proceedings involving accused arrested by agencies such as the Mumbai Police, Customs, Crime branch, directorate of revenue intelligence (DRI), state excise department, the CBI and few police stations."We have been protesting for the last one year. Initially, we submitted representations to the judiciary and also approached chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , who had assured us of assistance. However, several months have passed without any progress. After making repeated representations and meeting several delegations, we have now decided to go on an indefinite strike across the state," a federation member said.The federation has been agitating since September 16, seeking approval for a proposed revision of pay scales.The demand has gained momentum, with the Maharashtra State Judges Association extending its "full and unequivocal" support to the employees' demand in October.In its statement, the judges' association said employees of District and Subordinate Courts play a vital role in the administration of justice by maintaining judicial records, handling court administration and performing various allied judicial functions.Their responsibilities and workload are substantial, and the efficient functioning of the justice delivery system depends considerably on their services.The association termed the demand for pay parity legitimate, fair and justified, stating that the pay and service conditions of judicial employees should be brought at par with similarly placed employees of the high court establishment in keeping with the principle of equal pay for equal work.
Article Summary: Around 34,000 employees from District and Subordinate Courts in Maharashtra have gone on an indefinite strike. The impact was visible at the Esplanade Metropolitan Magistrate Court at CST. The strike is expected to disrupt day-to- day judicial work, including remand proceedings.

Article Title: Mumbai's Juhu beach sees 5-fold spike in garbage after Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Juhu beach collected 150 tons of garbage after Chhath Puja celebrations.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: Juhu beach saw garbage collection surge fivefold to 150 tons on Monday, a day after Chhath Puja celebrations drew thousands to the shoreline. The figure was 120 tons above the beach's average daily collection of 30 tons over the preceding eight days. The celebrations, which draw thousands to the shoreline for rituals and prayers, leave behind large quantities of waste, including flowers, food and other ritual offerings, contributing to coastal and marine pollution if not cleared promptly.An official said cleaning operations could not begin on Sunday evening, despite staff being ready, as the beach was packed with people, leaving no room for workers or machinery. "A conservative estimate puts the crowd at no fewer than four lakh people. We saw people beginning to gather from around 3 pm on Sunday, carrying mats and other seating arrangements to secure their spots. There was simply no space to even stand, let alone deploy cleaning staff and machinery. We could therefore begin the clean-up only after sunrise on Monday, once the crowds had dispersed," the official said.The clean-up began in full swing around 8.30 am on Monday and continued into the evening, with work still underway at 6 pm. Even additional manpower and machinery could not significantly speed up the operation, given the volume of waste. "We had brought in additional workers and machinery expecting to clear the beach faster. However, the scale of the clean-up meant even these additional resources could not speed up the process as much as anticipated. We will eventually clear the entire stretch, but restoring the beach to its usual condition will take considerable time," the official said.Discarded coconuts, flowers and sugarcane were among the waste strewn across the sand.
Article Summary: Juhu beach collected 150 tons of garbage after Chhath Puja celebrations. The figure was 120 tons above the beach's average daily collection of 30 tons over the preceding eight days. The celebrations leave behind large quantities of waste, including flowers, food and other ritual offerings.

Article Title: Take further steps to stop dog-bite incidents in Kandivli hsg cluster: HC to BMC
Article Text:
Mumbai:
